- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add slight upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.3–1.0), model often misjudges direction; favor mid-range forecast unless sentiment is strongly trending.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias to avoid bottoming too early.
